scope: Already-authorized service test execution using primary host runtime capability; does not grant new action authority or product ownership.
rules: Service worker remains sole product/test/evidence writer. Primary host may execute a reviewed exact test command against named disposable frozen staging and capture stdout/stderr/exit only.

Before a host test, worker supplies exact command, staging root, source/test/fixture input manifest and intended writes. Manager reviews actual code and bounds; host rehashes immediately before execution. All writes must be confined to disposable staging/runtime or named local process state, not product, canonical Task or worker evidence files.

Worker must not change the handed-off stage while host executes it. Independent authored source may change only when clearly excluded from the frozen stage; such runs are historical unless their input hashes still match final accepted outputs.

Use direct current source-byte compilation where required; -B alone prevents pyc writes but not stale pyc reads. Apply same actual loaded-byte provenance gates to test bootstraps and real service startup/replacement.

Host returns actual executor attribution, command, exact input hashes, return status and safe captured output. Worker records its evidence from those actual observations without claiming it executed the host command.

No credentials/bootstrap values in command strings, outputs or evidence. Test processes are owned, explicitly stopped/reaped unless a named approved browser-test session needs a live listener, whose ownership and cleanup must be explicit.

The current child socket.bind EPERM is a runtime capability limit, not missing user scope authority. Do not repeat escalation prompts for this known boundary; prepare host-executable batches instead. Other ordinary safe child work continues under its actual permission policy.

Final delivery requires current direct runtime tests for every14 SERVICE_PACKAGE criterion, including HTTP isolation, race/bootstrap provenance, queue/time/RSS, cancellation/session isolation, health/CLI and installed production assets. Initial smoke proves none of those broader gates.
